title: Geometric stalks of finite locally constant sheaves of sets are finite
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on its small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Assume $\mathcal F$ is *finite locally constant*: there is a jointly surjective etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ and, for each $i$, a finite set $S_i$ and an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\underline{S_i}$ on $(U_i)_{\Et}$, where $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is the restriction $V\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\to U_i$ etale, viewed over $Y$ through $u_i$, and $\underline{S_i}$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $S_i$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then for every geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the geometric stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite set. This includes the case $S_i=\varnothing$.

source.place: Definition Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), sets part (4); Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3), for stalks under restriction; Remark Tag 03P5 (remark-constant-locally-constant-maps), constant sheaves of sets (the argument there is written for groups and uses no group operation). The finite-stalk consequence is agent-formulated.

proof.text: *Lifting $\bar y$ to a member of the covering.* Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point. The morphisms $u_i:U_i\to Y$ are etale and jointly surjective, so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] there are an index $i$ and a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_i$ (same field $\Omega$) with $u_i\circ\bar u=\bar y$. Fix them and write $U=U_i$, $u=u_i$, $S=S_i$, and $\varphi:\mathcal F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline S$ for the given isomorphism of sheaves on $U_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03PR (lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover), applied to the covering of Definition Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) (3)

proof.text: *The stalk of the restriction maps onto $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$.* Let $\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ and $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ be the categories of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar u$ in $U$ and of $\bar y$ in $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]; the stalks are $(\mathcal F|_U)_{\bar u}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar u}^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal F|_U(V)$ and $\mathcal F_{\bar y}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal F(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], with germs $[s]^U_{(V,\bar v)}$ and $[s]_{(W,\bar w)}$. (a) *The map.* For $(V\xrightarrow{p}U,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ the composite $u\circ p$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2) and $(u\circ p)\circ\bar v=u\circ\bar u=\bar y$, so $(V\xrightarrow{u\circ p}Y,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar y}$; a morphism $h:(V',\bar v')\to(V,\bar v)$ of $\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ is a $U$-morphism, hence a $Y$-morphism, with $h\circ\bar v'=\bar v$, i.e. a morphism of $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$. Since $\mathcal F|_U(V)=\mathcal F(V\xrightarrow{u\circ p}Y)$ with the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$, the maps $\mathcal F|_U(V)\to\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, $s\mapsto[s]_{(V,\bar v)}$, are compatible with the transition maps of $\mathcal N_{\bar u}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the universal property of the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a map $r:(\mathcal F|_U)_{\bar u}\to\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ with $r([s]^U_{(V,\bar v)})=[s]_{(V,\bar v)}$. (b) *Surjectivity* (the reindexing in the proof of 03Q1 (3)). $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so $\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is filtered and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1) every element of $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ is a germ $[s]_{(W,\bar w)}$ with $(W\xrightarrow{q}Y,\bar w)\in\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ and $s\in\mathcal F(W)$. Let $V=W\times_YU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p_1:V\to W$, $p_2:V\to U$; $p_2$ is etale as a base change of the etale $q$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Since $q\circ\bar w=\bar y=u\circ\bar u$, there is $\bar v=(\bar w,\bar u):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ with $p_1\circ\bar v=\bar w$, $p_2\circ\bar v=\bar u$, so $(V\xrightarrow{p_2}U,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar u}$. Its image in $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ is $(V\xrightarrow{u\circ p_2=q\circ p_1}Y,\bar v)$, and $p_1$ is a $Y$-morphism with $p_1\circ\bar v=\bar w$, i.e. a morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ of $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$. By the cocone property of germs, $[s]_{(W,\bar w)}=[\mathcal F(p_1)(s)]_{(V,\bar v)}=r\bigl([\mathcal F(p_1)(s)]^U_{(V,\bar v)}\bigr)$. So $r$ is surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3), proof, third equality: 'the pair $(U,\overline{u})$ and the map $a:U\to X\times_YV$ corresponds to the pair $(V,a\circ\overline{u})$', for the etale $u:U\to Y$, whose inverse image is the restriction (Section Tag 03S2, paragraph after Definition Tag 03S3: '$j^{-1}\mathcal G(U')=\mathcal G(U')$ for $U'$ etale over $U$')

proof.text: *The isomorphism $\varphi$ on stalks.* The morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F|_U\to\underline S$ and its inverse induce maps $\varphi_{\bar u}:(\mathcal F|_U)_{\bar u}\to\underline S_{\bar u}$, $[s]^U_{(V,\bar v)}\mapsto[\varphi_V(s)]_{(V,\bar v)}$, and $(\varphi^{-1})_{\bar u}$ in the other direction (universal property of the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the maps $\varphi_V$ being natural in $V$); their composites agree with the identity on all germs, hence are the identities by the uniqueness in the universal property. So $\varphi_{\bar u}$ is a bijection $(\mathcal F|_U)_{\bar u}\cong\underline S_{\bar u}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

source.place: Definition Tag 040R (definition-stalk): the stalk is a colimit, hence a functor of the sheaf

proof.text: *The stalk of $\underline S$ at $\bar u$ has at most $|S|$ elements.* Let $P$ be the constant presheaf $V\mapsto S$ on $U_{\Et}$ (all restriction maps $\mathrm{id}_S$) and $\theta:P\to\underline S$ its sheafification, so that $\underline S$ is the constant sheaf with value $S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] (with $T=U$, $\bar t=\bar u$) the induced map $\theta_{\bar u}:P_{\bar u}\to\underline S_{\bar u}$ on stalks (colimits over $\mathcal N_{\bar u}^{\mathrm{op}}$) is bijective. The pair $(U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}U,\bar u)$ is an object of $\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]; let $\sigma:S\to P_{\bar u}$, $a\mapsto[a]_{(U,\bar u)}$. $\sigma$ is surjective: $\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1) every element of $P_{\bar u}$ is $[a]_{(V,\bar v)}$ with $(V\xrightarrow{p}U,\bar v)\in\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ and $a\in P(V)=S$; the structure morphism $p$ is a morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(U,\bar u)$ of $\mathcal N_{\bar u}$ (a $U$-morphism with $p\circ\bar v=\bar u$), and $P(p)=\mathrm{id}_S$, so $[a]_{(V,\bar v)}=[P(p)(a)]_{(V,\bar v)}=[a]_{(U,\bar u)}=\sigma(a)$. Hence $\theta_{\bar u}\circ\sigma:S\to\underline S_{\bar u}$ is surjective and $|\underline S_{\bar u}|\le|S|$ (for $S=\varnothing$ the stalk is empty).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) (2), stalks commute with sheafification; Definition Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) (1) for sets; the stalk of the constant presheaf computed from Definition Tag 040R (definition-stalk) and Lemma Tag 03PQ (lemma-cofinal-etale)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 2 and 3, $r\circ\varphi_{\bar u}^{-1}\circ\theta_{\bar u}\circ\sigma:S_i\to\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ is surjective, the composite of the surjection of step 4, the bijection of step 3 and the surjection $r$ of step 2. Since $S_i$ is finite, $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ is finite, with $|\mathcal F_{\bar y}|\le|S_i|$. As $\bar y$ was arbitrary, every geometric stalk of $\mathcal F$ is finite.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 03RU (sets), 03PR, 03Q1 (3) and its proof, 03PT (2). Steps: lift the geometric point to a member U_i of the covering (leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift); the stalk of F|_{U_i} at the lift maps onto F_ybar (the reindexing of neighbourhoods in the proof of 03Q1 (3), written out with W x_Y U_i; only surjectivity is needed and proved); the given isomorphism with the constant sheaf is a bijection on stalks; the stalk of the constant sheaf of sets with value S_i is the image of S_i (stalk of the constant presheaf, every neighbourhood maps to (U_i, ubar), plus sheafification preserves stalks, leaf lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk); conclusion |F_ybar| <= |S_i|. No new node: every non-definition node cited is a Mathlib leaf. The abelian lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk and lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction were not used (abelian only); lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ would need a sets version of the restriction/inverse-image identification, so the 03Q1 reindexing was written directly. Statement kept; added the citation [def-weil-geometric-point] and its stmt_dep. lean.statement: theorem finite_stalk_of_finite_locally_constant_sets {Y : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) (hF : ∃ 𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.etalePrecoverage Y, ∀ i, ∃ S : Type (u + 1), Finite S ∧ Nonempty ((F.over (𝒰.etalePrecoverageToEtale i)) ≅ (constantSheaf (Y.smallEtaleTopology.over (𝒰.etalePrecoverageToEtale i)) (Type (u + 1))).obj S)) : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y), Finite ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.obj F)
